targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-964 (2026-08-29, diagnostic) does NOT bear on MECH-482. Its load-bearing C2 ('the downstream consumer can change the committed action') was unsatisfiable by construction given the substrate state the run reached. All three seeds ended with n_targets == 1 and last_n_targets_matched_at_readout == 32 == K, i.e. every candidate matched the single target. EpistemicDeficitAccumulator.readout returns torch.where(matched, deficits[nearest_idx], 0), which with one target yields the SAME value for every candidate; StructuredCuriosity then applies total = total - weight * lp_vec (structured_curiosity.py:541-543), and subtracting a constant from every candidate score cannot move an argmax. yoked_divergence_frac == 0.0 was therefore mathematically forced and carries zero information about the mechanism. Note also that C1's PASS bar (>=1 persistent target AND >=1 update) is met at exactly n_targets == 1, the value at which C2 must fail -- the two criteria are not independent. The instrument itself is sound: the self-yoked control C3 was bit-identical as required, and n_readouts was 13/20/12 (non-zero), so the readout path really was exercised. The self-routed label 'accumulator_live_but_never_changes_committed_action' is literally true but reads as a fair test of selection-relevance, which this was not.

recommended_substrate_queue_entry.title: Give the epistemic-deficit accumulator a reachable multi-target regime, and gate its validation on per-candidate differentiation
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: EpistemicDeficitAccumulator.reset() clears all persistent targets every episode (deliberately, mirroring StructuredCuriosity's per-episode LP-EMA clear), so in 60-step episodes it never exceeds one target and readout() returns a constant vector that cannot move an argmax. Either lengthen the accumulation window / relax the per-episode clear for this sub-flavour, or run the validation in an environment that produces >=2 distinct uncertainty loci per episode. Separately, record StructuredCuriosity._last_lp_dev_range (max-min of lp_contrib) in the manifest -- it is already computed and is exactly the number that decides whether the per-candidate read can differentiate.

arguments_withdrawn.argument: The vacuous_readout_rate gate is blind: driver lines 223-227 return 0.0 when n_readouts==0, identical to 'never refused', so the readiness gate would pass on an accumulator whose readout was never invoked at all.
arguments_withdrawn.withdrawn_because: NOT the cause here -- n_readouts is 13/20/12, non-zero on every seed, so the readout path was genuinely exercised. The gate defect is real but unexercised by this run; recorded as a latent instrument finding rather than a diagnosis.

learning_extracted: Two criteria are not independent evidence when one's PASS threshold is set at the exact value that makes the other unsatisfiable. C1 ('>=1 target') and C2 ('the read can change selection') stand in precisely that relation: at n_targets==1 the readout is constant and no argmax can move. A readiness gate for C2 must require per-candidate DIFFERENTIATION (>=2 matched targets, or a non-zero lp deviation range), not mere non-emptiness.

A negative control establishes specificity, not sensitivity. C3 (self-yoked, bit-identical) proves the divergence detector does not fire spuriously; nothing in this design proves it CAN fire. A positive control -- inject a synthetic two-target deficit and confirm the argmax flips -- would have made the zero interpretable in one cheap step.

RECORDING GAP: StructuredCuriosity already computes _last_lp_dev_range = lp_contrib.max() - lp_contrib.min(), the exact quantity that settles whether the per-candidate read can differentiate candidates. It was not recorded. Recording it costs nothing and would have made this diagnosis self-evident from the manifest.

The driver imports assert_no_structurally_unsatisfiable_gate, but that guard is static over pre-registered specs and cannot see a degeneracy that emerges from the runtime state reached (n_targets==1). Structural unsatisfiability needs a runtime check too.
